body: This is an ethically driven conservation project run by Dudley and his family. There are some amazing turtles to see here, mostly in their own tanks, to show visitors and to raise awareness about the odds stacked against the survival of these graceful and beautiful creatures. For some species a critically endangered status makes the odds even lower. There is also a hatchery where eggs are buried and, when hatched, released into the sea. If you’re lucky, you might witness a turtle release on your visit. It’s a wonderful experience. The family invite volunteers from around the world to help them run their project and learn about their conservation efforts. I am currently volunteering at the sanctuary offering visitors tours of the project. If you want to know more, pop by and see what it’s all about. This project is sometimes mixed up with another sanctuary down the road - but this is the real deal! Where prodding, poking, feeding or touching the turtles is prohibited. The address….13/A Galle Road, MahapalanaKosgoda, 80570 Sri Lanka Please contact them in advance to make a booking….email - kosgodaseaturtle@hotmail.comTel - +94 71 209 3929Website - https://kosgodaseaturtle.org

body: I’m sat here daydreaming about my recent amazing trip to Sri Lanka. I had such a great experience and memories which will last a lifetime. I don’t do ‘normal’ holidays, I like to do something meaningful. This is my 3rd trip using The Great Projects and once again they didn’t disappoint. So, for my recent week off I volunteered at the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project looking after and learning about the endangered sea turtles that visit the area. What Dudley and his family/team are doing for the sea turtles is truly incredible. The conservation project was established by Dudley Perera over 35 years ago. They survived the terrifying Tsunami in 2004, where the project was virtually wiped out, but they’ve kept going with the support from locals and volunteers. They have come back stronger, and now they are able to provide more care and protection to keep the visiting sea turtles safe and give the hatchlings the best start in life. The main aim of the project is to monitor local sea turtles’ activity and conserve their local nesting sites. They collect and rescue eggs found locally and hatch them within the safety of the protected hatchery on site. The project has a small number of young turtles on site which they keep for a short amount of time i.e., 3-4 years before they are released into the sea. They call this ‘headstarting’ they are kept to educate local residents, school children and international visitors, demonstrate how important it is to protect these creatures before it’s too late. Unfortunately, there are several hatcheries in Kosgoda, and the majority are attractions, using turtles to make money rather than protecting them. I can confirm that the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project is very passionate about protection of the turtles, from hatching all the eggs they receive and releasing them back into the wild. I received such a warm welcome from Dudley and his family/team when I arrived. They took me under their wing, and I instantly felt like part of the family/team. Even though I was the only volunteer at the time, if anything this helped me get stuck in, I even gave up my free time to help where I could. The food and drink they provide was amazing, traditional with some western options on occasion. The accommodation was perfect, conveniently located across the road from the project and the air con was a relief. Now let’s talk about the day-to-day activities - During my short time at the project, I completed a wide range of activities; Tank cleaning (inc pumping fresh water from the sea), feeding the young sea turtles which they look after for a short time (up to 4 years old before they are released into the sea), collected hatchlings from the hatchery after they dug their way out of the nests, cleared some of the older nests which hatched a few weeks ago, this consisted of digging with your hands and clearing the old shells from the nests, scrubbed the signs, helped paint and write a new sign, general tidy up removing plastic following the strong winds and occasional rain and we released hatchlings into the sea under the safety of our presence keeping away predators like birds and wild dogs every night. Wishing them good luck on the long hard journeys ahead and wondering one day the females may come back to lay their eggs. Dotted throughout the packed day’s work I provided tours of the project to visitors from all over the world, I’d show people around, explaining what the project does for the turtles from egg to release into the wild as quick as possible, explain the differences between the turtles and even highlighting the different turtle personalities (they have some cheeky chappies). I found this part of the project work extremely rewarding, the gratitude I received from the visitors across the ages and nationalities was lovely, made me feel I was doing good, helping spread awareness of the project and the need to protect these wonderful animals. I did miss out on a couple of things during my stay, this was due to my timing which was at the tail end of the season, but I still had the best experience. I did however miss out on witnessing a mother laying her eggs, I missed this by 3 days, but you could still see her tracks in the sand. And burying eggs, that Dudley had brought from local fishermen who find nests and sell to him to bury and hatch rather than selling on. But to be honest there was so much to see and do this would have been a bonus, my experience was still amazing without them. I would even consider visiting the same time next year. If like me you want to do good by volunteering, I highly recommend visiting the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project they genuinely need our help to keep these turtles safe, what they are doing there is amazing, and I’d love to give up my office daily job and move there for good. Address: No. 13/A Galle road – look out for the bright blue wall 😊

body: We volunteered at the Kosgoda Sea Turtle project as a family of four for a week. The work that Dudley and his family do to educate local communities and school trips on turtle conservation is invaluable. The project has been running for 35 years, looking after and caring for injured turtles. The main aim of the project is to educate communities on endangered sea turtles and the importance of keeping beaches clean. Dudley has a true passion and commitment to this cause and has been working with turtles all his life. Yes, the sanctuary is small and you could say it is in need of an upgrade but the tanks are meticulously cleaned each week and the turtles in residence are well cared for with a lot of love and hard work. The money made from tourist visits is put back into rescuing turtles. Eggs that are collected by poachers for the restaurant trade or black market are intercepted and brought to the sanctuary where they are reburied and cared for until hatching. They are protected from predators by nets and released at sundown, close to the sea to ensure they have the best chance of survival. Dudley and his team are extremely knowledgable and work so hard for the cause. Dudley and his family went above and beyond to make our stay unforgettable. We were all very sad to leave and we hope to be able to return in the future.
title: Unforgettable experience

body: My wife, myself and our two young boys spent a week volunteering at the Kosgoda turtle sanctuary and had an amazing experience learning how Dudley and his team are helping preserve all the sea turtle species in the area. The work this centre undertakes greatly increases the chance of survival for the sea turtles and is helping to educate the local population on how important it is to look after the environment and also the turtles. The small donation to enter the sanctuary goes a long way to help look after the turtles and there are also opportunities to pay extra to release turtles on an evening, back into the ocean which is an amazing experience. Dudley was such a brilliant host and his wife cooks amazing food, if anybody would like to try a volunteering experience with a young family I couldn’t recommend a better place, Dudley also arranged day trips to other areas of the island during our free time, he was an absolute legend and made our holiday in Sri Lanka so special.
title: Excellent volunteering experience

body: Never visit this place. The only thing to see here are few dead baby turtles and an arrogant ten year boy handling the ticket counter. He refused to give us tickets saying they are for guests but charged Rs.250 each to enter.
title: Terrible place

body: A place that has a reputation for the conservation of turtles. While quite dowdy to visit, it is a "shack" on the beach the work that is being done is fantastic. The person who showed us around was obviously very enthusiastic about the work being done and passionate about the damage being done to turtles by fishing nets and plastic. The maimed turtles being cared for is a lesson to learn from. I suggest a visit just to show how as humans we impact on the lives of other animals.
title: Needs to be seen from an environmental perspective

body: My husband and I had a great time. Dudley was very knowledgeable and you can really tell he cares a lot about the turtles. title: Amazing place

body: Great family run project to save turtle population. Mr and Mrs Perera and their team have been great running the project. Any student need work experience this is a place to do the work experience.
title: Amazing place to get project experience

body: In short a wonderful experience. They patiently answered all our questions and explained the steps they take to preserve the eggs and turtles. This was followed by a truly heart warming experience of releasing baby turtles into the sea. We were each given about 15 turtles to release.The project conserves all possible species of turtles but majorly the Green and Olive Ridley turtles were present during our visit. We were blessed to see the hatching of eggs and release the young ones into the sea by hand.
title: Wonderful experience

body: VolunteeringI had originally booked two weeks volunteering with the project but I enjoyed my self so much that I stayed for an additional week. And I could really stay forever. Dudley and his family make the experience. Nothing was ever too much trouble and they would all go above and beyond to ensure each volunteer has everything they need. As an Animal Science in the UK I wanted to see first hand conservation work and feel part of making a difference. I feel like I have achieved this. Not only have I buried eggs and released hundreds of babies whilst volunteering at the sanctuary , I have also spent a lot of time giving tours which has not only improved my knowledge on Sea Turtles but also means I have spoken to lots of people about the importance of conserving these amazing wild animals.The main message of the project is conservation and sustaining and improving wild populations. By educating the public, carrying out beach cleans, burying eggs so that they can hatch safely. And releasing babies, means the project is making a big difference to wild population numbers. AccommodationStaying at the project really felt like a home away from home. The accommodation is clean with air con, Wifi and lovely social area and garden. The food was traditional Sri Lankan meals, which I will be cooking when I get home, which included breakfast, lunch and dinner. The trip was my first adventure alone and meant I was very anxious at being in a new place. I definitely didn't need to be as anxious as I was! And I really do feel like part of the family and will be returning at any chance I can. The staff were friendly and so helpful and it has ben so enjoyable meeting and working with different people. Meeting the other volunteers has also been a great experience and i have also made a best friend for life. Along with lots of other friends. And I am so grateful to have shared this life changing experience with them, where i have made unforgettable memories. I will miss the entire family so much. And i am already looking forward to returning. Dudley and his family are doing wonderful things, not only in the sanctuary and the wild population numbers but also to the volunteers they welcome in. The family really do make the experience. Along with providing the chance to play a big part in the conservation of endangered Sea Turtles.
title: Volunteering

body: I volunteered at this project for a month and it was the best experience! I was travelling alone in Sri Lanka but immediately Dudley and his family made me feel so welcome at the project and I settled in straight away. I felt so cared for, the food was incredible and it is a lovely living environment for volunteers. The volunteer house was clean, very close to the sanctuary and felt very homely! Beds were comfortable and I slept very well. As a volunteer we also participated in regular beach cleans which was great as it felt good to actively take care of where the mother turtles were coming and laying their eggs, making a difference in their safety and conservation of their environment.As a visitor, you get to see how well the turtles are cared for, whether they are older rescues or baby turtles that have hatched and will be released back into the wild. I would definitely recommend booking to release baby turtles which was very popular for tourists and is such an amazing experience as it is done in the evening and the sunsets are incredibly beautiful! Thank you all so much for making my time here so amazing! I enjoyed every second and will definitely be returning.
title: Amazing experience definitely recommend!

body: This sea turtle conservation centre is doing great things to ensure that the injured and resued turtles live out their lives as comfortably as possible. The actual centre looks a bit rundown but it's all run on charity donations from visitors and I honestly believe that the people working there love the turtles immensely. It's worth a visit to fall in love with the guests that are lucky enough to be rescued and cared for in this place. Then there's the little newly hatched turtles that are adorable too. Altogether a lovely experience and definitely worth a visit to experience these majestic beauties. Any donations are helping to keep this project on track and ensuring there is help at hand for any needy guests...Tagimuri Clan from Cumbria UK...
title: Amazing experience

body: Sea Turtles are one of threatened species of the world. Southern costal line is a common place for laying eggs by sea turtles. Victor Hasselblad sea turtle conservation place is the first most sea turtle conservation place in Sri Lanka started in 1978. It is a good place to experience hatchlings and sea turtles.
title: A good place to visit

body: Visited on 21 February 2020The turtle conservation project undertaken by Sri Lankan Govt. is commendable and many organizations have come forward to support the cause. Well funded both by the local govt as well as by global fund raising the project is a success.The hatcheries have trained workers and they keep records of the conservation work done year on year.We visited one of the hatcheries and found the experience very satisfying.Support this environmental cause.
title: Commendable and Relevant Effort

body: This place is well worth a visit to see real conservation in action. From hatching to release, these guys are very careful to preserve as many Turtles as they can. As well as the whole process of hatching and releasing Turtles, there are a lot of other things to understand about the work here. Please make a visit, buy your ticket (and if possible make a donation) to make sure that this vital work continues.
title: Great Conservation Project

body: Dudley began this operation as a young man over 30 years ago and he, his family and a small team run the sanctuary with dedication and efficiency. This includes encouraging locals to bring the eggs to them where they receive a fee per egg to give them a chance rather to survive rather than selling them at the markets for food. The work they and other sanctuaries in the area are doing for sea turtle conservation is amazing. We were told by one visitor that this is the best one in the area. I was as a volunteer for a week and was involved in all aspects of turtle care and conservation and seeing all aspects of the life cycle of these amazing creatures. I also helped out with general maintenance and showed tourists and school groups around to share the plight of these amazing sea creatures and the ongoing conservation efforts. It was a truly rewarding experience. It is a very well run sanctuary and I encourage you to visit (or volunteer) which helps contribute to their work.
title: Volunteering at the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project

body: My dad and I went on a spontaneous trip here and were the only ones to be there at the time. The main guy Santha is only too pleased to show you around personally and gives great explanations of all the turtles, history and the conservation work they do. They are doing vital work to protect baby turtles from being eaten / killed and gives them best chance of survival before they are then released back into the ocean. They are also caring for disabled older turtles who would die in the wild on their own. It costs a LOT to run the project every day and every visit / donation is visit - please visit if you get a chance! Also some lovely dogs to see who they also rescued :) as a dog lover - this was a bonus! It is wonderful to see that there are some good people out there trying their best to do what they can for animals and conservation - it is NOT easy! And a full time life work!! Admiration !!
title: Wonderful visit! Learnt loads and great work being done here

body: This is an educational experience that shows you why conservation of turtle species is required, the impacts of plastic in our oceans etc. You see at close hand a number of turtle species, I saw day old turtle hatchlings. I was a little bit concerned about holding one because I did not want to cause any distress to the turtle but trusted the guide. The part of the project that impressed me the most was the care provided for disabled turtles, either those born with shell deformities or one blind turtle who required hand feeding and those with injuries caused by fishing methods etc. Please choose to visit this project rather than those facilities just there to allow tourists contact with turtles. The tuk tuk drivers all have their preferred projects relating to commission they receive so please ask for this specific project if you are in the area, only 500 rupees to enter.

body: I would highly recommend to visit the conservation project when you visit Sri Lanka. It is amazing to see and hear what they do for the turtles! The guides were very nice and good with the explanations! I think I‘ve learned alot about turtles after the visit. Gogogo

The facility also houses the injured turtles until they are well again (injuries caused by fishing nets, predators etc) and makes a home for the deformed and permanently injured turtles.We were allowed to hold a baby turtle and see an albino turtle. I would definitely recommend a visit if you are on the West Coast.

body: Today I visited Kosgoda turtle hatchery and wow what an experience! We saw lots of baby turtles which had been placed under sand in a secure environment until they were ready to hatch. This is done to protect them from predators and poachers. Once the baby turtles have hatched they are shortly released back into the ocean within a day or 2, this was something I had the pleasure of doing, the baby turtles hatched earlier in the day. Kosgoda turtle conservation also tries to rehabilitate injured turtles with the intention of re releasing them back into the sea. Unfortunately this is not always possible due to their severe injuries meaning they would be vulnerable in the open ocean. Kosgoda turtle hatchery relies heavily on entrance fees and donations as sadly some turtles require medical treatment at veterinary hospitals due to wounds from plastic and netting. This is a family run project with the help of volunteers and I honestly think they are doing a fantastic job! The young man who walked us around was very genuine and showed a real concern for the turtles wellbeing along with the effects the hatchlings being poached has on our environment/oceans. He was very knowledgable and spoke very clear English, clearly a huge animal lover as also had a few friendly dogs. I just want to say a huge thank you for this special experience and also keep up the good work, it will pay off!

body: We visited yesterday after having researched several places along the south coast and speaking to locals. At first it seemed pretty sketchy, we walked into an outdoor covered area where there was a large tank with no water in, several tanks with water and turtles in and several people all doing things. No one greeted us except for a hello so we thought perhaps we were at the wrong place and were just looking at turtles in tanks but after a short while one of the people came over and took us to where the eggs are planted to start the ‘tour’.We were told how the eggs are laid on the beach, they then take the eggs and ‘plant’ them in their secure enclosure, label them and keep them safe. When the eggs hatch the babies are put in a fairly large (in relation to their size) tank where they are looked after until they are ready to be released into the sea. Instinctively the babies tended to crowd at the end of the tank closest to the sea. We were invited to hold them and were told it does not harm them nor cause stress. Inside this tank was also one month old turtle, I’m not sure why that one hadn’t been released. In the other tanks were larger turtles, in an ideal world the tanks would be larger as they did not seem large enough based on the size of the turtles but these were mainly injured turtles so in the wild they wouldn’t survive. Some were missing flippers after shark attacks so would never be released but others were recovering from broken flippers having been caught in fishing nets before being released again. There was an albino who wouldn’t be released as it lacks the camouflage needed for the wild. During the tour the empty tank was being filled with water, apparently we visited when they were changing the water in the tank. This tank had two huge turtles and one smaller one in, again based on the size and nature of the animals the tank would ideally be larger but ideally the animals would also not be injured. All in all I would recommend this place, the entry was 1000 rupees.

body: I did a 1 week volunteering at this lovely sanctuary. Our weekly activity includes educating the guests on turtle conservation and ensuring that the tank is clean. No chemicals were used when we cleaned the tanks. We drained the dirty sea water into the sea and then pump fresh seawater into the tanks.We used sand to scrub away the moss and algae.We also helped out in feeding the turtles. Each adult turtles eat once in 2 days. Baby turtles eat every day. We also engaged in scrubbing the turtles' shell with a brush. I was trying to not hurt them as I read that they have nerves on them so the shell is not like our fingernails. Other activities include removing any roots in the hatchery as the roots can impair the hatchlings' movement and growth under the sand. On wed afternoon, we taught English. Mon-Weds' afternoons should be on English teaching but Mon and Tuesday was 24th and 25th Dec so it was a holiday period for the children.The best thing that ever happened were eggs that were found on Christmas Day! I had the privilege to bury the turtle eggs on Christmas Day. We continue to bury eggs every 2 days or so. In the wild, 1 out of 100,000 turtles (0.001%) made it to adulthood. With the efforts of this sanctuary, there is protection from predators so the survival rate is 95%! So now is 95 out of 100,000 which is 0.095%I waited almost everyday for the green turtles eggs buried on 14th Nov to hatch. This was because on hotter climates, they would hatch in 40-45 days instead of 2 months. I left the sanctuary on Sunday morning at 7.30 am i.e. Day 45. And they hatched on the very day too, from what I read from the other reviews! Wish I could witness the emergence of hatchlings and their release into the sea in future!This sanctuary is an established sanctuary as it has been around for 30 years. It does not allow touching and holding of the turtles. Places that does this are not genuine sanctuaries as it is unethical to put animals in distress, just to cater to tourists' preference. No flash photography is allowed as it distresses the turtles too. Some turtles, especially females are kept to allow them grow for ~ 5 years as the sanctuary aims to increase the survival rate. As turtles grow bigger, the number of natural predators drastically reduces to just the tiger shark and the killer whales. The main culprit for dwindling populations are human activities. So if all is well without human activities, they can live up to 100 years.So I continued to emphasise on the need to conserve the environment and give these beautiful creatures a chance of a wonderful life!
title: 1 week volunteering

body: I have been there with my family on the way to Matara. In this center they treat and protect turtles before release to the ocean. This one of the best conservation project around Kosgoda area.
title: They Do A Excellent Job

body: An enjoyable visit lasting about 45 minutes. The owner’s son showed us around and was very knowledgeable. He talked us through the variety of turtles and why there’s a need to conserve them. We were fortunate to see c70 turtles being born, which is unusual as this apparently normally happens when it is cooler at night.
title: Turtle conservation

body: Although the French volunteer who was our guide was very knowledgeable and what she said was Informative, we found the whole place rather basic and not very inspiring . The conservation that takes place is good but so much more could be done to make the visit more enjoyable. It was, honestly, rather boring. The tanks the turtles were kept in were small and inadequate. I understand that funding is a problem. A small shop selling turtle merchandise could bring in so much more income. Lots more needs to be done to make the place more child and tourist friendly and interactive.
title: Disappointing

body: Kosgoda is on the west coast of the island not too far from Galle. It is a wonderful place to see and even hold turtles. The staff are friendly and very well informed and display a real love of nature and the environment. We even had the chance to hold 1 week old baby turtles and were invited to accompany them on the boat to release many back into the wild. They have around 6 or 7 different species including a full grown albino turtle which would never have survived in the wild. They also keep several disabled turtles which again would not survive in the ocean. The visit does not last too long but is both educational and informative. Highly recommended.
title: Fantastic to see and hold turtles!

body: It was a unique experience seeing a bunch of day-old turtles swimming around. We were even allowed to hold a 3-day-old turtle in our hands and experience the weird sensation of having them crawl on our hands. The turtle hatchery rescues turtle eggs from the beaches (even buying them from fishermen) and hatches them in a safe environment protecting them from predatory birds and helping protect turtles and grow their numbers. The baby turtles are then released into the ocean. Any handicapped/injured adult turtles are also protected and kept in the hatchery and used to educate kids and visitors. One of the 20-year-old turtles weighed over 40 kgs and it was quite a task carrying it to see its weight!
title: Interesting experience..

body: The place is actually a good place to visit and nice experience which you wont be able to get from anywhere within the country. You don't have to plan a separate visit for this as you could only have to spend about 30 mins there. They do really care for these creatures especially the care they give for the disabled ones was amazing.
title: Following the absolute meaning of conservation

body: I didn't give it a full 5 stars because it didn't compare to an experience we had in a different country where we stayed up at night to watch a mother sea turtle nest and helped the conservation center collect her eggs. But still, this center gives you a great intro into what kind of work this center does. Even though some people may take issue with holding a few of the turtles and their eggs, my son and I loved being able to be that close to nature. It was great to see and learn about the different kinds of turtles at the center, of all ages (no leatherbacks though- not the right season now). Plus, our guide wasn't too commercial, unlike many other places we had gone to as part of our southern Sri Lankan tour. If you're in the area and have some time, stop by.
title: One of the best things to see in the area

body: SeaTurtle Conservation and research centre, the oldest in the country and the beach Kosgoda is where the conservation and research helps saves sea turtles..every night the rescuers collect the eggs , places them in protected sand , once they hatch, baby turtles are directed to the light into the hatchery and by day 3 released back to sea. The kids had an amazing time . While the facilities were basic, the guides and volunteers were so passionate about their work. We were most humbled the the experience..
title: An amazing and educational experience for the whole family

body: They negotiate on the Entry rates. Once you enter you get to see several varieties of Turtles.. from babies that are one day old to Loggerheads which are above 20 yrs of age
title: If you have nothing to do go to this place..... worth a visit

body: One of the best experiences while in Sri Lanka. The place at first glance is not so impressive - small place with 5-6 water tanks beside the beach. But they have a wonderful collection of turtles from 2 weeks old to 70 year old. The coolest thing this the guy will actually allow you to touch and hold the turtles. Some of the older ones are huge and very heavy so u need to be careful while holding them. They even have very rare albino turtles. They have a place where they hatch the turtles - the eggs are perfectly round and resemble golf balls - u can hold them too. My 6 yr old kid had an amazing time.
title: Amazing place for kids

body: Whilst the entry to this conservation project was a little steep, it does go to a good cause. That said, getting hit up at the end for a "donation" after we had come as a group of seven (no child discount), was a bot rich.That aside, our time at this facility was well spent. We were able to handle some of the turtles, which our children loved. The guide also provided excellent information regarding the turtles, their habitat and also the efforts being undertaken to conserve them at this, and other, facilities.The drive was a good 40-50 minutes west of Galle, but it was well worth it.
title: We learnt a lot about turtles and the effort to conserve them

body: Turtle Research & Conservation Project, Kosgoda - Visited this particular turtle project as it was recommended by the Lonely Planet guide and not too far from where we were staying. A great family experience - very informative and interesting; ended up spending a fair bit in the onsite gift shop (good quality stuff!). We paid extra to release baby turtles into the sea at sunset - that was something special. Highly recommended!
title: A Great Family Experience

body: We visited the turtles late one afternoon/early evening. The guide was really informative and answered all of our questions. We then got the chance to release some of the turtles into the wild. I would definitely recommend. Agree with the comments that the tanks could be bigger.
title: Trip to see the Turtles

body: We visited this wonderful place with VTS Lanka Tour Guide - Mr.Rohan, and most amazing part of this visit is touching the baby turtles and hold on big turtle. it was great experience. thank you Rohan again
title: Amazing Place

body: We volunteered for the day and got stuck into scrubbing the tanks. We learnt about the different turtles, including the residents: green turtles, loggerheads, hawksbills, olive ridleys and although they didn’t have one, leatherbacks. With our doubt the 5 tiny green turtles we released at sunset was unforgettable.Magic.Dudley and Presantha were lovely and we mentioned we hadn’t eaten hoppers so they made hoppers for dinner. So kind.
title: One day of wonder

body: This was a visit of less than one hour but it was an inspiring one. The facility was wiped out in the tsunami but they are now looking after newly hatched turtles in huge numbers and returning them to the sea when they are three days old. Some injured adults and albinos are there permanently. A great visit and a large and interesting shop.
title: Wonderful work project

body: What a great place to visit. The care they show for the turtles is amazing and the tour they give of the place is excellent. You even get to pick up a baby turtle.
title: Amazing

body: We had a great time visiting this place. Best moment was releasing the little turtles to the sea in the evening. We had a five year old who had an awesome time.
title: Good experience

body: We stopped off at the turtle hatchery on our way down to Galle. We were shown around by a helpful guide who spoke very good English. He explained all the amazing work they do to help with turtle conservation. We were able to see and hold the very small turtles that were waiting to be released back into the sea. This is a very worth while project and I was happy to pay the small amount asked for the ticket to support their work.
title: Worth a visit

body: So happy and proud of the work being done at Kosgoda. The area is small, but you get the opportunity to see hatch nests, baby sea turtles (before they are released), as well as a few more grown individuals who are not able to be released. There is a very nice souvenir shop as well.
title: I Cannot Even Begin to Thank These People Enough

body: Seeing the facility, learning about turtles, and getting to release baby turtles into the Indian Ocean were trip highlights. They also care for injured, disabled, and albino turtles that would be at risk in the open water. The work they do is important.
title: Amazing experience

body: The turtle hatchery is definitely worth a visit. Tickets costing 1000 rupee each (£5) for a twenty min trip doesn’t seem over the top for us at all, but it is simply a short visit. The Conservation is there to protect the turtles eggs, injured or endangered turtles. You get a guide who gives you plenty of information about the project and turtles themselves. Whilst getting to hold 1 day old turtles, see the egg hatcheries, hold larger turtles and stroke albino turtles (they have soft shells so love it apparently). They do expect a tip at the end, it is suggested its donations to improve the facilities however our tip never made it in to the donations box so not too sure about that. You can return at 5.30pm and for an extra £10 release baby turtles in to the sea! Definitely worth a visit, such a lovely way to start or finish your day!
title: Worth a visit

body: Enjoyed our visit to this facility, and hopefully helping the sea turtles to survive.Our guide was helpful and informative about the turtles, although he didn’t know anything about the history of the facility or the effect of the tsunami. He also couldn’t explain exactly why the turtles were better in the facility than in the wild.Nevertheless, we loved seeing them and learning about their habitat etc.Well worth a visit.
title: Very interesting visit, and loved the turtles

body: Great place to visit. It was good to see the work they are doing to protect and look after these turtles. The guide knew a lot about them and the information was very informative. It was so nice to see them up close. The beach view at the back was breathtaking. A worthwhile place to visit.
title: Very interesting

body: This place is wonderful - amazing to get so close to such amazing animals . Six year daughter was soooooooo happy to have held a baby turtle too
title: Loved it

body: It was maintained but expensive in context of turtle available and price they have charged us.English speaking guide was okay.Before buying tickets one should enquire about available turtles inside.
title: It was okay

body: We went there in around 6:20 pm. First we’ve been told it’s 1000rs/person, I just said “is it 500 or 1000?” Then suddenly it became 500 rs/person! And there were many types of cheap paper tickets, and i think I could have a lesser price but I didn’t bother to be honest. When we entered, there was like 8 big turtles only, but a lot of small ones. We didn’t hold them as we didn’t encouraged to do so by the lady who was showing us the place and give us information about the turtles types and so ( i felt like she was in hurry, maybe because of our late arrival in their closing time- but not an excuse!). You can make donations if u want to. Overall, I didn’t find it interesting and a must do thing. If u have time you can do it. We did and hopefully it will be used for the good cause. Our tour here took only 10 min!
title: Good to see, not a must!

body: One of the most valuable activity of this project is its hatchery .They are collecting eggs & nesting . If you wish to donate money for them to collect eggs will be a very valuable thing you can do in your life.Collected and rescued eggs can hatch safely away from predators before being released into the sea.Only few hatchings from each batch will ever mark it to adulthood .It's a nice & educational tour for our kids and they enjoyed lot.
title: CONSERVE THE BEAUTIFUL CREATURES

body: As you enter this Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project , you can just see how terrible conditions exists in this business model. The printed entrance tickets they sell are all bargain able, they reduced the price to me 25% discounts. The travel agent or taxi driver who takes you there has commission from these hatcheries.One of the turtle has one of his arms cut, may be due to brutalities of these keepers. The whole setup is to cheat tourists and make money on torturing the turtles. Do not visit them to be part of their crulity to these mute animals.
title: Scam in name of Turtle Conservation

body: If you're planning a trip to the south of Sri Lanka and want to fill your itinerary, this is the place for you, your friends, your family, your grandmother, your uncle! Hear me out.So I was a planning an itinerary for my friends and while planning for Galle, I found out it was short and there was more to be filled besides going to museums, eating, shopping, etc. Then I found this place.Yes, I was sceptical because some reviews are putting me off but I still added this to my itinerary.So foreigners are LKR 2,500 for releasing the turtles and getting the information you need, if you don't want to release turtles, if you're a foreigner, it's less than that. The releasing of turtles is around 6.15pm - 6.30pm. I recommend heading there before this time if not you will have to go on the next day. Let me tell you, what an amazing and unforgettable experience! Before the release of turtles, we're given a very informative information about the turtles from the volunteers, their species, etc. Then we waited for 30 minutes because we arrived around 5.30pm.I also recommend going there bracing yourself because my friend chickened out when she saw the baby turtles ;) Overall, it was an amazing experience, you could be that one friend who has done this while the others, not so much.
title: Sceptical? Want an unforgettable experience?

body: Im not usually taken by captive animal attractions, however this appears to be a genuine attempt to help improve the survival rates of sea turtles. The guide was very knowledgeable and we didnt feel pressurized to spend or donate more than we wanted to
title: Appears to be doing good work

body: Spend 30 mins to understand the turtle's lifecycle. This is very important for living in harmony with nature.My kid had a nice time here learning about different forms of turtles.
title: Very good experience

body: Visited this place after long time.Entrace for locals is Rs50.They have small turtles in tanks, which are kept for 7 days before they get released to the sea.In other tanks you can see few rare species
title: Save them for Future

body: It was interesting going to this conservation project, I think it's great what the volunteers do, dig up the eggs so that the babies can hatch in a safer environment but you end up feeling sorry for the turtles that are more grown up and don't have much space to swim around. I was told that they would be killed if they were let out in the wild but the solution in my eyes would be building a bigger space for them to swim and not confining them to a concrete box.. I did feel as though the people care about the animals but wild animals in a small space should have more options..
title: Interesting

body: There are numerous Turtle Conservation & Hatchery places and we chose this one based on reviews and convenience. It was very much worth the stop and price of admission. We spent about 30 minutes here and it was really cool, esp seeing the little hatchlings! Family run and a great way to get a couple of tourist dollars into well intentioned locals who work hard.
title: Great Visit!

body: Really a good place to visit. You get information on the entire life cycle of turtles. Once the turtles are ready, they are released into the sea. Only the deformed, sick and injured are cared for life.
title: Turle hatchery and Conservation center

body: This place is amazing. It is all about turtle conservation and not about making money. They take such good care of the turtles and it’s refreshing to see people with such a love and commitment to these special creatures. We are able to hold baby turtles that are just 3 days old and doing so was so emotional for me. It was amazing! I would recommend this to anyone.
title: Best thing I have ever done!!

body: This place was great. The guide was very knowledgeable and gave us a heap of insight into the sea turtle situation in Sri Lanka. We got to release 15 baby Turtles into the ocean. This was such a beautiful experience. Our 5 year old son enjoyed releasing the Turtles and getting to see all the different Turtles as well. I would definitely recommend visiting this place if you can.
title: Awesome

body: The turtle hatchery located in Kosgoda is famous for several species of turtles, specially the endangered hawksbills. Eggs which are left uncovered on beaches all around the coast are brought by fishermen of Kosgoda area, which has led to the hatching and release of 100,000 young turtles in only two years since the hatchery opened.
title: Sea Turtles

body: Very worthwhile stopping in for a look They are passionate about turtles. There are egg farms incubating eggs and at 3 days old the turtles are released back into the sea. Even get to see Albino turtles and hold baby’s.
title: Great experience

body: We visited the centre in the morning and the guide patiently explained to us the efforts being taken for conservation of sea turtles. It was great to see the 1-3 days old baby turtles swimming in the concrete tanks. You get a chance to hold them for a few seconds and click pictures. There aren’t too many volunteers and the place gets crowded making it difficult for the staff to keep an eye on all visitors. The beach surrounding the centre is pristine and the water is a deep shade of blue. The souvenir shop was a tad expensive.
title: Good experience

body: We went there in the afternoon and it was a good experience to see a different kind of turtles. Even they allowed us to release little turtles and it was fun for kids. They were handling turtles well and learnt a lot about turtles and their conservation project.
title: Good Experience...

body: It was a wonderful experience to release the green sea turtles and watch them swim out to sea. However, I didn’t like seeing the large turtles in their small concrete enclosures as it restricted their movements. While I was there a few busloads of local students arrived and ran around madly putting their hands into the water. Needed more people to supervise.
title: Turtles

body: This foundation allowed us to release baby green sea turtles. It was a truly amazing experience. For a small amount of money we were able to help, in a small way, these magical creatures. Xx
title: Turtles

body: Not overly impressed with the volunteers. Had visited another Conservation project and got lot more information and shown things in more detail,
title: Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project

body: My husband and I visited the hatchery in late January - We were amazed by the wonderful people we met there, protecting and looking after the turtles.We learnt so much from them - and the visit was both interesting and informative.I would highly recommend a day trip there for a couple of hours.We had turtles coming ashore onto the beach at Ahungalla, where we stayed - and we saw where some eggs had been laid in the sand - it was stunning, and we felt very privileged.If you are looking for an honest, reliable and good value guide to take you there - Look up Manu on WhatsApp 0094 72471 5703He lives just up the road, and is a terrific guide. We highly recommend him taking you to the hatchery - as we had the best time there.
title: A must visit place in Sri Lanka

body: We were inspired to visit by the positive reviews, and our experience did not disappoint. We visited around 5.30pm and were shown the different types of turtles by the female guide who was very helpful. We were not allowed to touch the turtles which was very good, except the baby one who needed the warmth from human hands to grow. Then at 6.15 we were given a bucket of baby turtles born that same day to release by the water, guided by the expert staff. However, an eagle was circling overhead so we retreated and waited around twenty minutes for darkness to fall and the eagle to return to its nest. Often the eagles eat the babies! But luckily when we did release our baby turtles made it to the sea. It was wonderful.
title: A wonderful experience

body: We visited the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation project as part of our last day in Sri Lanka on a wildlife tour. Our guide at the centre was very informative and it was great to see the baby turtles albeit in tanks, but hopefully that is securing a better start in life for them! We were able to take photographs and handle some of the older turtles, carefully under the supervision of the guide. All in all a worthwhile project and we were glad to donate to this cause at the end of our visit. They do have a fairly good souvenir shop on site as well, which they say contributes towards the cause. We did buy a t-shirt for our niece, not least because they were cheaper there than we had seen in shops in Galle.
title: Great experience

body: We visited Kosgoda STC after recommendations from our driver. We found ourselves on a 4KM stretch of beach, at sunset. We spoke with the Grandson of the owner, who gave us the history of the project. The staff were really knowledgeable and clearly loved the work they did. Lots of volunteers keep the beaches clean and ensure these creatures are kept safe. We entered the project and were presented with baby turtles, whom live here for 3 days before release to maximise their chances of survival. We then saw a variety of injured turtles and talked about the work the centre does with universities. I feel that some of these turtles could be released and perhaps do not need to be there, however the majority of the work here is excellent. At sunset, we released around 12 turtles into the sea, which was amazing! I would highly recommend.
title: Impressive work and a wonderful experience

body: We visited Kosgoda turtle project for my birthday. I'd researched a few hatcheries because I wanted to make sure that we visited one that had good welfare standards. I firstly emailed the project and had a very welcoming reply from Dudley who confirmed that they would be releasing baby turtles on the day that we wanted to visit, so we booked a visit and to take part in the releasing. The project is funded by donations and we were welcomed by a British volunteer who was very informative and was happy to answer all of our questions. They have 5 or 6 tanks with adult turtles of different sub species, including an albino turtle. You are NOT allowed to handle the turtles - which we were very happy about from an ethical point of view. They also have a hatchery where they buy eggs from fishermen and they hatch the eggs in the safety of the project - they're covered in netting. The turtles are kept for a few days to gain strength and give them a better chance of survival in the ocean. The beach there is absolutely beautiful and we also enjoyed a walk and a paddle before sunset which is when the turtles are released. They naturally hatch and enter the sea at this time of day. For the release we were given a bucket of baby turtles and then we walked down to the sea with them. Releasing the turtles was absolutely magical and we'll never forget it.
title: A great experience

body: We visited in the late afternoon when you can release turtles into the sea, which we did (1000rupee on top of the 2000 entry fee). Our guide was knowledgeable and spoke better than average English. Made us realise the damage plastics are doing to our sea creatures 😯
title: Surprisingly good

body: We visited the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project and the tuk tuk driver took us to the wrong turtle place. We kept showing him the map and called Dudley to go to the Kosgoda Conservation Project. Don't be fooled and go to one where they touch the turtles, they aren't for conservation. This one is on the main road and on the beach, not hidden in the back streets. Dudley talked to us about the reality of sea turtles, how fisherman dig up the eggs and sell the eggs for food (a repetitive cycle) and how he is trying to educate children on sea turtle Conservation and to stop this behaviour for the next generation. We saw a school bus of children arrive while we were there which was nice and the children were very excited to learn. He was very informative on our visit and they are really trying to do the best they can by donations from tourists and education. They keep some of the turtles in concrete pools so people like us can visit and appreciate the turtles before they are released into the ocean. He has some larger turtles which swim around in large concrete pools and a disabled turtle that can't be rehabilitated for normal life. There are other turtle farms around the area but they are all for the wrong reasons and for the donation of 1000 rupees you can visit and learn about them. For a donation of 1500 rupees you can help release the baby turtles on the beach at 530pm in the afternoon. Amazing sunset and experience. Dudley is doing the best he can. I loved visiting here and it is a must to help support turtle conservation! Look for the Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project sign on the main road. Ask for Dudley and don't support the other turtle farms who are doing it for the wrong reasons. Watch your map when you go with the tuk tuk drivers.
title: Go to Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project on the main road with Dudley

body: we were a group of 13 visiting the hatchery.the manager chandrsiri abrew was very generous with information on turtles.. the probems faced by them..the harm humans and predators cause.. the protection given to the healthy, sick and handicapped turtles.we saw all types of turtles.we also bought items from their shop to help a cause.must visit.
title: informative and heartrending

body: We took a tuktuk here from bentota, takes about 15-20minsIt is better to go early evening between December and April when they release the babies into the sea We arrived about 5.30 and immediately asked if they had any turtles to release, and luckily they had over 50. Two of the volunteers there were english university students who took us around the tanks for about 15mins, showing us the work they do, also showing us turtle eggs and going out onto the beach to see turtle tracks and holes dug by the turtles. Just as it got dark about 6.15pm we helped release the turtles, we were given a bucket with some in, amazing experience, although halfway through a sea eagle appeared and so we had to gather the babies up again and wait for the eagle to move offSomething we will never forget doing1000rupees (£5) to go in, and another 1500 to help release the babies.Worth every penny IMO
title: Absolutely must do this

body: Wonderful place to see the baby turtles come out and grow into big ones before they take off to the sea
title: Cute turtles all around

body: It's interesting place to see the turtles and you can see the staff is working really hard to protect the turtles' habitat. A nice little place to stop by on the way from Colombo to Galle.
title: Nice detour on the way to Galle

body: We visited the conservation project on a rainy day as it was covered. The staff are very friendly and kind to explain how they take care of the turtles. I'm some cases they even let you touch/hold them which is very nice. Having worked in animal rehabilitation myself I can very much apriciate this type of work and fully support their work. Certainly recommend to visit.
title: Nice visit with friendly staff.

body: We visited this hatchery on Jan 29th 2018 on way to Bentota. Guide gave us description. Few water tanks having different age turtles,few malformed turtles also. They purchase eggs from fishermen, bury those. After hatching release in sea. Ticket is LKR 1000,very costly. Washrooms not good here.You are not allowed to touch.
title: Good Turtle Conservation Initiative

body: Very good work, they help the turtles to survive and to edjucate the people about the danger of their extinction. There are a lot of young volunteers, which is even more interresting. It is nice to see someone care and it is nice to see people to give the gifts for the right think. The clean and well prepared area for the turtles and the turtles eggs. I recomend the visit.
title: Alma

body: This is a small conservation project run by some very sincere people. The conservatory had about 5 water tanks - where different turtle species are on display. Additionally, there are 3 tanks dedicated to raise the hatch-lings before they can be released back into the sea. It was fascinating to see the beginning of the life of these turtles who on an average will go onto live for 100+ years. We went as a group of friends and had a great time understanding turtles and their behaviors. It's a small project and you can easily get done under an hour.
title: Amazing to see the beginning of life of the magnificent creatures

body: The entrance fees was too much and there was not much to see. Did not like the place at all. The guide did not have much information. It looked like a con for tourist.
title: Not worth the money & time

body: We enjoyed the experience to learn, play and explore their natural environment the little sea turtles. The place is located by the side of the prime road and it is very easy access through any mode of transportation.
title: Great experience

body: A great private initiative with focus on the care and preservation of sea turtles. We were given a tour by a young employee/volunteer and it was amazing to see how they cared for them.Keep up the good effort.
title: Very Noble Initative!

body: Ever considered lending a hand with the birthing of sea turtles, or perhaps take part in releasing these new explorers into the wild? For three decades, Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project has played a crucial role in providing a promising beginning for baby turtles and the best part? You can assist in helping these beautiful creatures have a hopeful beginning.The first hours of newly hatched turtles are critical, riddled with danger including predators, obstacles and even misdirection to land. The center purchases eggs from locals to ensure a better future. Once the eggs arrive, they are buried and sign posted indicating the date, species and quantity of eggs. After 2 months of incubation, you can be the first view for these hatchlings, and if that isn’t enough, actually play a hands-on role in releasing the infants into water.Located off the coastal road (A2) in Kosgoda and only 100kms (62mi) from Colombo, lies one of the coolest experiences I had in Sri Lanka, and one I can assure you, you will never forget.
title: Uh, can you help with some baby sea turtles? Yes please!

body: Great initiative but dont think it was explained well. There were 4 tanks and few turtles. A brief was given and that was the end of it!
title: Interesting initiative!

body: So nice to visit a place were you really felt that number one priority were the turtels not to get money from tourists. We were educated by a nice lady and Learned a lot about these amasing animals.
title: With focus on whats best for the turtels

body: AUTHENTIC: is the word that describes the project and the staff managing it. The project has sincere motives and the people managing it are sincere. One must donate and buy buckets to release the turtles in the sea, helps the project sustain iteself. Loggie is a disabled turtle and needs all the care and support. My 14 years old daughter got very inspired by spending time with Loggie the turtle at the project. She is writing a fiction story around Loggie and plans to donate part of the proceeds to the project. She will be happy to donate 5 copies of the book to 10 schools around the world: She is self funding the publishing. We all must ask everyone to visit the Kosgoda Project and add lot of value to them. Enjoy the sunset from the project, watch the turtles with excitement and let your kids bond with you over this amazing experience
title: LOGGIE: DESERVES IT ALL @ KOSGODA SEA TURTLE PROJECT

body: Amazing what these people do and the amount of turtles they have saved. A very informative and worthwhile visit.
title: very interesting

body: I love the idea of conservation and protecting all species. This program is great to help increase the survival rate of the 4 kinds of turtles found in the Indian Ocean. We released 10Green turtles. They were 3 days old.
title: Amazing experience

body: The hatchery buys turtle eggs from fisherman and buries them on the property, taking care that the eggs hatch and the turtles are released into the sea instead of the eggs being eaten (delicacy in Sri Lanka). There are three types of turtles there, and the baby turtles are kept in tanks for a week before being released. Turtles with deformities or disabilities are kept in the tanks for life for teaching purposes since they will become easy prey in the ocean.It’s fantastic that the turtles get a chance at life instead of being eaten as eggs. On the other hand, the turtles that are kept for life in the hatchery have a poor quality of life with small tanks and little space to move around. They don’t get to go in the sand at all, not even occasionally. I have mixed emotions about this place.I feel that the volunteers / workers need to be better informed about the turtles and the project. They didn’t have answers to a lot of basic questions we asked. In one room, there are paper clippings regarding the project. A lot of the stuff is in the local language and not translated. body: A superb week volunteering at the project with our three sons (12, 14 and 17). We all spent the week cleaning, feeding, collecting, releasing and generally caring and getting to know a lot about the turtles, the local people and the balance of conservation and survival. Taking visitors on the tours was fun and meeting a myriad of different people, cultures and attitudes to the turtles and the conservation theme was an education in itself. The boys certainly developed their confidence and appreciation of the challenges conservation faces globally. We also cleaned the beach on a couple of occasions and in five minutes filled up a bin bag each - but one decent tide and the rubbish (mainly plastic bottles and fishing boat detritus) was filled back up.The comment about handling the turtles was a discussion between ourselves and the other volunteers (from France, Germany and China). We had all seen poor incidents of children and adults poking and plaguing the turtles as well as the real delight and true care that being so close created for many. It's a balance and we made up our own rule that we would monitor and allow touching for those that showed genuine interest and care as well as respect (usually when it was quieter) - not perfect but we felt better. It's also one of the things that brings people in, generates income, and allows Dudley, the owner, to buy more eggs off the locals who are encouraged to see the conservation and preservation of turtles as a financially as well as environmentally valuable asset. All in all its a great project and well worth the visit as the volunteers are great (😀) and the cause is worthwhile. It's also worth knowing that the majority of turtles will be released into the sea once they have recovered from injury or before they are 6 years old as they will be too big. Finally Loggie, the disabled turtle, is doing well and enjoying her tuna and swimming strongly in her tank but will never venture out as she would not survive. A visit to keep the place open for her alone is worth it.
title: Volunteers for a week

body: Kosgoda is about 30 kms from Kalutara and is near Bentota.There are several places in the Kosgoda area for turtle conservation. These white turtles have a genetic deficiency due to Albino.The mating to laying of eggs take 14 days. The eggs look like TT Balls and of similar size. These eggs are inside the sand for 48 days before they hatch and the baby turtles come out. There are three ponds which hold 1 day, 2 days and three days old turtles. body: We were wary of the many turtle farms and hatcheries in Sri Lanka, most of which seem to have little care for conservation and are purely for profit, so we did a lot of research and found this to be exactly what we wanted - education, animal welfare and conservation. We took a tuk-tuk from Hikkaduwa (about 50mins and 4000 rupees for the round trip) and passed many dodgy looking turtle farms on the way which our driver insisted were where everyone wants to go. Luckily we had a map and photos of this place on my phone so we were able to find the right one. We were given a tour by two volunteers, one from Wales and one from Australia, who showed us around and introduced us to all the turtles, ranging from 4 days to 6 years old green, olive ridley and hawksbill. The volunteers gave us loads of information about the centre and its conservation work and knew loads about the different breeds of turtles and the personalities of some of their longer term residents. We spent a good hour after the tour just going around looking at them all, especially the tiny, four day old green turtles, and it was well worth the trip. I even god a squirt in the face from one of the older hawksbills - super cute! Even our driver came and had a look around and seemed to enjoy it so will hopefully bring others back here, although he kept saying that the other one was bigger!Highly recommend this place, animal welfare is prized above anything else and you're not allowed to pick up or touch the turtles which is encouraged elsewhere. You can still get really close and take great photos and videos without stressing the animals. I am glad that the tickets cost for our visit (1000 rupees each, about £5) will help them continue their good work. It's worth checking if they will be releasing any hatchlings on the day you visit as you can pay a little extra to help release them on the beach. We texted via the number on their website ahead of our visit but unfortunately weren't in luck on the day we chose. Avoid the horrible turtle farms, go here and rest assured that you will be helping conserve these little beauties. Thank you for a memorable visit 😊
title: Perfect, happy turtles

body: This is a wonderful stop on the coast road between Galle and Colombo. Firstly, Kosgoda beach is beautiful and worth a look on its own. The sea turtle project is the highlight of the stop (and there are several along the road in close proximity, so make sure you stop at the right one). The odds against sea turtles surviving to adulthood (5 years) are staggeringly low (somewhere between 1 in 1000 - 10,000), due to natural threats, destruction of habitat, and human threats. This has lead to critical declines in turtle populations around the world. This projects gives them a hand with as little human intervention as possible. The group works with local fisherman and buys eggs that they would have otherwise sold as food, and works to hatch them, and at about a week old, sends the wee little turtles out to sea. We had a wonderful tour from a volunteer, who was willing to answer as many questions as we had. We weren't there in the evening to see any babies go to sea, but I can imagine that would be a wonderful experience. 1000 Rupees in support of these efforts is more than reasonable!

body: We enjoyed our visit to this Conservation Project. It is heartwarming to know that some people do care about the turtles. We were shown how they let the eggs hatch and then how they are set out to sea after 3 days. We were able to see various types of turtles. The gift shop is not very interesting, they should have some nice tee shirts for sale, that would sell well. The quality of the gifts was not too good. Otherwise a good place to stop.
title: Very interesting visit

body: We decided to visit the Sea Turtle conservation Project as we were touring in Sri Lanka, but the tuk tuk driver at the station took us to the wrong place, a "turtle farm". The place with a turtle-shaped entrance, where they ask you to pay 1000 Rps for the ticket is the WRONG place. The Sea Turtle Conservation Project will only ask for 500 rps. BE VERY CAREFUL ! We were horrified to see the tourists being allowed to hold the turtles and take them out of their pools. Some of these "turtle farms" are REALLY WRONG and not treating the turtles correctly. It is WRONG to hold or manipulate a turtle, you can hurt it and it can be dangerous for your own health. Don't trust any tuk-tuk drivers when you arrive at the station. You really have to go to the right place and be in touch with Dudley and his team of volunteers, they are doing a GREAT JOB. Turtle Farms can be HORRIBLE, please be sensible and make sure you go to the right place where turtles are really cared for ! And remember : DO NOT HOLD THEM !
title: BE CAREFUL - DON'T MISS THE RIGHT PLACE

body: who in the world would dedicate their life to caring for a blind turtle all of their life? Theres a person here who does precisely that!
title: caring people

body: You don't need to book an expensive tour, the ticket in includes a very informative guide around the hatchery, where the process from buying the eggs from the fisherman through to the releasing the turtles is explained. Great conservation work all through ticket sales and donation. A must do
title: Great work

body: A short and nice trip educating you with the different turtles and their history and upbringings will make you feel with the tremendous efforts the persons in charge are putting to make this conservation successful. Do pay a visit!
title: Best Place

body: One of the most important activities of the project is its hatchery. Within the sanctuary of the project, collected and rescued eggs can hatch safely away from predators before being released into the sea. In addition, a certain number from each hatching are kept back for a short period for 'headstarting' before release.
title: Kosgoda Sea Turtle Conservation Project

body: There are several turtle conservation places on the west coast of Sri Lanka, though what we heard from the locals is that the Kosgoda Turtle project is the best.The guide was good, gave us detailed information of turtles as well as their project. He let us play with the turtles, let us pick up the large ones as well. It was a very interesting experience and a very noble cause by the project. Must visit..!!
title: The best one in the nearby areas

body: My first time at A Sea Turtle Conservatory. The Mother Turtles arrive on Kosgoda Beach in the Dark to lay their eggs and never return again.The Eggs are Incubated for 3 days before the little ones are released into the Indian Ocean - also after sunset. Sadly only 20% survive - the rest are devoured by predators.This site In Kosgoda also takes in injured or physically deformed turtles and looks after them.Staffed purely by volunteers.Personally speaking I found this visit very educational and thoroughly enjoyable - and of course was trigger happy with my IPhone....
title: Very Educational and Informative

body: Informative visit. Kids enjoyed carrying the baby turtles. Guide was clearly knowledgeable about his field, and English as medium of communication was efficient. Good conservation initiative
title: Educational fun

body: This is a great place worth a visit if you live nearby in Induruwa. Or if you pass by going north/south. Not worth a long trip. Friendly and knowledgeable guides speaking a good English.
title: Nice small place with good guides

body: The guides are volunteers from around the world so you'll have pot luck range with knowledge provided. Key thing is that they won't force-release babies to sea.... no eggs had hatched when we were there so there were no babies to release. The guide discouraged handling the babies as well. Informative information was provided re feeding, daily handling, washing etc. This is a voluntary service so any donations and entry fees are used specifically to help with the upkeep of the site.
title: Short, but sweet

body: Inexpensive family activity that is interactive and educational. You get to pick up some of the turtles and all of the tour guides are very knowledgeable. Takes about 30 minutes total so keeps the kids attention just long enough.
title: Great for kids and parents

body: We walked to the location from the Riu Hotel covering the distance in about 25 minutes.We've seen turtles laying eggs at nightime on beaches elsewhere during our travels but this time we were able to hold young hatchlings being cared for & studied for scientific research prior to release into the ocean . Also injured turtles being nursed back to health so they can go back into the sea .We had a one to one discussion with a very informed member of staff & spent an interesting hour listening to him telling us about their conservation work .Your entrance fee & any extra donation helps to the upkeep of the project. If you're interested in the preservation of endangered species then this will be a worthwhile place to visit.
title: Interesting visit

body: It was maybe a 20 min visit where a local man took us around the unit showed us new hatched turtles to the ones ready for release at day 3. We saw the various disabled and injured turtles and listened to horrendous tales of poaching. It was short but our guide was funny and endearing. The conservation project release the babies nightly having salvaged the eggs. Worth a stop off if you are passing for sure.
title: Short but fun

body: we enjoyed our visit very much and had a lot of information given to us. we had a good guide whom explained a lot, very informative
title: lovely

body: Had an amazing experience volunteering at kosgoda turtle conservation and the only thing I would change is that I should of stayed longer! The best turtle release to visit if you are travelling around sri Lanka and would like to see one. Very informative and sustainable - and you can get involved with releasing turtles in the evening.
title: Amazing experience

body: Entry fee is 500 LKR per person and it is worth visiting as you get complete information of sea turtles. you can see white sea turtles which are very rare, just like white tigers. you can hold the baby turtles
title: had good experience of watching sea turtles

body: Besides seeing the sea turtles in the ocean, this is the second best place to see them. You can tell they was really well looked after which was great. The guides were very knowledgeable and their knowledge in different languages was amazing. You can tell everyone working here has a real passion for the sea turtles. I won't tell you everything but they did tell us they pay local fishermen for the sea turtles to stop them eating them. This is true dedication to what they do. Nothing felt forced and you was told after you'd seen the conversation that if you wished to donate then you could do. Any donation seemed very much appreciated which was lovely. It is such an amazing thing you are doing here and I'd recommend anyone to come and visit.
title: The best place to see sea turtles in Sri Lanka in the sanctuaries!

body: Nice place, you can see four kind of turtles, small baby turtles, eggs, albino turtle.. you can come and see..
title: Nice to see

body: A good place to visit😃amazing to see the turtels and a good guid that tell us about it😃you can also holding the turtels😃they are doing a good jobb for the animals! Amazing 😃
title: Renne

body: Interesting short visit/stop point for those heading down the coast to Galle. This was included as part of a private day tour, but the short presentation was informative with the opportunity to handle baby turtles and slightly larger ones. The logic behind the program was explained and demonstrated and we saw injured or birth defect turtles (albino) which are captive and would not survive if released. Whilst there is a bit of a drive to up sell the usual tourist souvenirs, there was no undue pressure and we left a small donation without buying overpriced items. All in all, well worth a stop off, Very informative.
title: Interesting, informative short stop on route to Galle

body: A fantastic place for all ages.They show us the eggs the picked up in early morning, the new born turtles, one day old, two days old. Big 35 years old turtles, disabled turtles and white albinos turtles. Fascinating!
title: Worth visiting

body: It has people to explain, but they run out of staff on some days, however, even on our own we enjoyed seeing this amazing creatures, who need our help to survive.
title: Enlightening

body: It's a small place with about 6 small tanks with few sea turtles and there is no body to explain about the turtles or the project. You will have to just go around by your own and see the turtles on the tanks by your own (no explanation and don't at least have a board with a description). Ticket is only Rs.50, not expensive but the time you spend to travel to visit this place is in vain.
title: Not worth at all

body: Had an amazing visit to this place. Not a government funded institution but rather a private venture.Was wiped out in the tsunami in 2004, but has been rebuilt.They seem to be doing an amazing job.Information and knowledge of our guide was impressive and he is quite passionate about the work they are doing.Initially sad to see them keeping blind and deformed turtles in the pens, but understanding that they would not survive in the wild, but then to use them to promote conservation and understanding of their plight balances this out.Highlight is the albino's (again would not survive in the wild). Their carpaces are just stunning.Only concern is being allowed to handle these magnificent creatures without washing hands. Would thoroughly recommend a visit to this one. There are many of these ventures in the area and clearly some exist to make money.

body: .Small but nicely done. gentle people around the turtles. Good informations. people offfers you to come as volonteers. You can release babies turtle to the sea in the evening...
title: very interesting.Small but nicely done. gentle people around the turtles.

body: The whole family was amused by the information been told at the place. We saw many different kind of turtles ( and their stages in life) who are healthy or has deformation. We were amazed to see a white turtle for the first time in life!
title: Very educational

body: This place contains an amazing creatures which are turtles and has few kinds you won't find anywhere else. Also it's base on the tickets which a 1000 LKR per person for buying food for the turtles. The guide wasn't that good but he was active and got our attention and he was doing his best to make our experience to the max. It's nice to know that such places exists to take care of animals.
title: A great place to visit and to know it exists

body: Only a small place but the guy who explained all about the turtles was very knowledgeable and answered all our questions. Given that such a small number of baby turtles make it to adulthood we have to support places like this who try to increase those odds. We need to educate stupid people who think turtle eggs and turtle meat are good to eat. We have to stop thosesame stupid people exploiting turtles for their shells for jewellery or decoration or supposed medicinal reasons. We have to encourage people who save injured turtles who have had flippers entangled in nets with a view to repatriate them to the sea when they are strong enough. Sure the place is not fancy and many turtles are in relatively small pools and some are clearly trying to get out but they will be in the sea again soon when given their clearance from the government welfare/agricultural officer.View it from those aspects please......this is not a petting zoo, these are still wild animals with no predatory instincts of their own but who need some human support at times.
title: Conservation is the key factor here

body: We were the only 2 visitors, but the person who took our money was not interested in answering our questions. There was a disabled turtle and several grown ones that were being kept captive for 'research'. The newly hatched were we were told being readied for release tonight, but that just drives the collection of funds to buy the eggs from fishermen. This is not conservation, but a tourist money maker!
title: Sad to see such beautiful creatures in such a place

body: We visited this place to see Turtles. There are so many turtles and the staff will explain you about the Turtle's life. You can touch the Turtles, they will allow you, but some of them are not allowed to touch.
title: Good experience

body: This was a well organised operation, with cooperation from local fisherman too. Knowledgable staff shared the work they do, starting with the hatchlings, through to release. Lots of sick and injured turtles were cared for and also some albino turtles were well looked after. The group ahead of us were French and had a tour specifically for them in French and ours was in English which was very good.A nice hands on experience with a decent gift shop too.Well worth a visit.
